text: One may find clean messy coordinates part project/work/etc. look fit workflow going way visualization? Let’s say following messy coordinates ’ve compiled different places, leading variety messy formats: Parse messy coordinates: Combine coordinates data. Coerce sf object Calculate center plot view Plot data using leaflet package Figure 1 ’d like data certain area, e.g., political boundary park boundary. can clip data bounding box using sf::st_crop(). First, define bounding box, visualize: Figure 2 Crop data bounding box: Plot new data: Figure 3
code: if (!requireNamespace("sf")) install.packages("sf") if (!requireNamespace("leaflet")) install.packages("leaflet") library(parzer) lats <- c(   "46.4183",   "46.4383° N",   "46.5683° N",   "46° 27´ 5.4\" N",   "46° 25.56’",   "N46°24’4.333" ) lons <- c(   "25.7391",   "E25°34’6.4533",   "25.3391° E",   "25.8391° E",   "25° 35.56’",   "E25°34’4.333" ) dat <- data.frame(   longitude = parse_lon(lons),   latitude = parse_lat(lats) ) dat ##   longitude latitude ## 1  25.73910  46.4183 ## 2  25.56846  46.4383 ## 3  25.33910  46.5683 ## 4  25.83910  46.4515 ## 5  25.59267  46.4260 ## 6  25.56787  46.4012 dat$shape <- c("round", "square", "triangle", "round", "square", "square") dat$color <- c("blue", "yellow", "green", "red", "green", "yellow") dat ##   longitude latitude    shape  color ## 1  25.73910  46.4183    round   blue ## 2  25.56846  46.4383   square yellow ## 3  25.33910  46.5683 triangle  green ## 4  25.83910  46.4515    round    red ## 5  25.59267  46.4260   square  green ## 6  25.56787  46.4012   square yellow datsf <- sf::st_as_sf(dat, coords = c("longitude", "latitude")) datsf ## Simple feature collection with 6 features and 2 fields ## Geometry type: POINT ## Dimension:     XY ## Bounding box:  xmin: 25.3391 ymin: 46.4012 xmax: 25.8391 ymax: 46.5683 ## CRS:           NA ##      shape  color                 geometry ## 1    round   blue  POINT (25.7391 46.4183) ## 2   square yellow POINT (25.56846 46.4383) ## 3 triangle  green  POINT (25.3391 46.5683) ## 4    round    red  POINT (25.8391 46.4515) ## 5   square  green  POINT (25.59267 46.426) ## 6   square yellow POINT (25.56787 46.4012) center_lon <- mean(dat$longitude) center_lat <- mean(dat$latitude) library("leaflet") leaflet() |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(data = datsf) |>   setView(center_lon, center_lat, zoom = 10) bbox <- c(   xmin = 25.42813, ymin = 46.39455,   xmax = 25.68769, ymax = 46.60346 ) leaflet() |>   addTiles() |>   addRectangles(bbox[["xmin"]], bbox[["ymin"]], bbox[["xmax"]], bbox[["ymax"]]) |>   setView(center_lon, center_lat, zoom = 10) datsf_c <- sf::st_crop(datsf, bbox) Warning: attribute variables are assumed to be spatially constant throughout all geometries leaflet() |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(data = datsf_c) |>   setView(center_lon, center_lat, zoom = 10)

title: parzer: Parse Messy Geographic Coordinates — parzer-package
text: Parse messy geographic coordinates various character formats decimal degree numeric values. Parse coordinates parts (degree, minutes, seconds); calculate hemisphere coordinates; pull individually degrees, minutes, seconds; add subtract degrees, minutes, seconds. C++ code herein originally inspired code written Jeffrey D. Bogan, completely re-written.
